definition: Expert–novice differences are the performance and attention differences seen between more highly trained people and less experienced beginners on the same task. In this packet, the term refers to findings that tactical training experience, more than time on the job alone, is linked to more efficient gaze strategies during stressful decision-making.

reasons: The first sentence defines “expert–novice differences” as “performance and attention differences” between “more highly trained people and less experienced beginners on the same task,” but the provided packet does not explicitly make or support that definitional framing.

The packet supports only a narrower claim: that “tactical training experience, rather than occupational tenure alone, contributes to more efficient gaze strategies under stress,” which is insufficient to justify the broader definition’s general wording about performance/attention differences on the same task.

The packet supports this term only in a narrow police use-of-force eye-tracking context; it does not establish the broad general definition about all tasks or the general claim of “performance and attention differences” between highly trained people and beginners.

“Performance differences” is not specifically supported in the packet; the packet’s support is for more efficient gaze strategies under stress and related decision-making findings, not a general performance-based definition.
